alignment.finding: the two issue-rate levels follow the loop head's address mod 32: heads at 6 (mod 32) issue 0.6088 ops per cycle per hart and heads at 22 issue 0.5814, a 4.71% difference with nothing in the data changing -- an instruction-FETCH alignment effect, measured off the same binary the campaign ran (physics skeptic, E61's physics review)
alignment.how: maximal runs of >= 24 packed-vector instructions are the unrolled loop bodies; the run's first address is the loop head. The c2 family is identified by its pinned third operand (ft7) and its opcode, which fixes its mode; the four df.addr kernels are identified by vs2 == vs1 (index-only work) and are counted, not named, since the emission order does not label them.

addr_count_check.note: the four df.addr kernels cannot be matched one-to-one to modes 306-309 from the bytes alone, so this is a COUNT match: how many heads sit at each residue against how many of the four modes run at each rate.

ipc.rate_finding: WHY THERE ARE TWO LEVELS AT ALL (the physics skeptic, E61's physics review -- re-derived here from docs/reports/data/2026-10-21-dtf/proof/enercat-df-aifoundry2.dis.txt, not quoted): the level follows the LOOP HEAD'S ADDRESS MOD 32. Over the 84 long packed-vector loops in the binary, the c2 family's four opcodes pin the map one-to-one -- mode 300 (fand.pi) head 0x8005802396, mod 32 = 22, 0.5814 ops/cycle/hart; mode 301 (for.pi) head 0x8005802206, mod 32 = 6, 0.6088 ops/cycle/hart; mode 302 (fadd.pi) head 0x8005802076, mod 32 = 22, 0.5814 ops/cycle/hart; mode 303 (fxor.pi) head 0x8005801ee6, mod 32 = 6, 0.6088 ops/cycle/hart -- so heads at 6 (mod 32) issue 0.6088 ops per cycle per hart and heads at 22 issue 0.5814, a 4.71% difference with NOTHING in the data changing. The four df.addr kernels cannot be named a0/a1/a3/a5 from the bytes, so they are a COUNT check and it agrees: 1 head(s) at the fast residue and 3 at the slow, against 1 of modes 306-309 at the fast rate and 3 at the slow. This is an instruction-FETCH alignment effect: it is why A2.1 found the rate fixed by the mode rather than by h, why it is identical on all three cards, why every rate gate had to be computed within one mode, and why the same mode can shift between builds (mode 179's +5.1% above is a relink moving its head across a fetch boundary). It is reported, never a gate: §9's own row says each shape's IPC is a REPORTED quantity.

board.reading: Taken as the registered statistic reads literally -- the pass as the unit of replication, no order term -- hi is EQUAL within 3 SE (|t| 1.43) and lo already DIFFERS (|t| 5.20). But the hi per-pass values track the pass parity (-1.02, +0.16, -0.90, +0.02): the block that runs SECOND reads +0.52 W higher, which inflates the naive SE sixfold. With that balanced order term fitted, the point estimate is unchanged at -0.44 W and |t| is 9.55 -- the two MESH halves are NOT electrically symmetric, by about 0.4 W out of the 12.5-14.4 W the work itself draws (~3%). This is a CROSS-CHECK on this card, not the registered tier-1 arm, which is family B on the pinned 600 MHz card.
board.registered_rule: E-D7 tier 1 (README section 9, row C58 C83 C84 C91): board power for d7w_hi and d7e_hi equal within 3 SE. This block is NOT the registered family-B half-die amplitude arm, which is measured on the pinned 600 MHz card; this is the same equality test read on the dtf-cam block's own meter at aifoundry2's 800 MHz / 0.618 V.

established: The pattern MOVES. Swapping which MESH half runs loud moves heat across the board by +372.9 mK on the double difference, p = 0.0007 against the registered cyclic null with all 10,000 labellings enumerated. The hub's prescribed regulator control is PASSED: two fixed voltage regulators cannot produce a pattern that changes sides with the shire mask.
It is a dipole, not a level shift. The card-mean of the difference image (the camera's own read of 'Delta P_card == 0') is -13.2 mK against a +373 mK half-to-half contrast, p = 0.96.
It lies on one axis. Halving the frame the other way returns -11.7 mK, p = 0.29.

It is not the block order. Decomposed on the balanced 2x2, the side term is +372.9 mK and the order term +23.6 mK; once the order term is out the four passes agree to within +/-2.3 mK (SE 1.16 mK on 2 df).
The hart activity alone already carries it: the quiet lo arm shows the same dipole in the same direction (173 deg vs 174 deg) at +202.8 mK, 54% of the loud arm's.
not_established: Which image half is the die's West. The camera's orientation relative to the MESH x<=2 split was never measured, so the finding is 'the image half at lower x heats when the 0x3131733b mask runs' -- label-blind, exactly as the tool's own sign_note says.

Any displacement in millimetres. No mm/px scale exists for this card, and from W-E alone a displacement is not identified in the first place (plan section 10, rule 8). The plan's '~11 mm' is untestable from this block.
Absolute mK, mK/W, or a die-side amplitude: the camera has never been calibrated on this card and the die-to-back coupling is unmeasured (plan section 10, 'what tier 2 cannot show' iii, iv).

The shire map. That the pattern splits where MESH says it should is consistent with the hart->shire->position map, but the halves-only resolution cannot test a single shire (section 10, ii), and the monopole's null SD of 216 mK is far too wide to resolve the 0.44 W electrical asymmetry the board meter does see (~34 mK expected).
Anything at constant TOTAL power. Both arms run half the chip idle, so this is a contrast at constant WORK, not the page's constant-total-power dipole (section 10, i).
camera.honest_reading: For an exploratory test this is about as clean as it gets: the effect is 2.8 null-SDs out on the conservative cyclic null and sits at or near the floor of the two other nulls, it reproduces in all four passes with an order-adjusted spread of +/-2.3 mK, it survives every assignment, warmup and detrend arm (+349 to +572 mK), it disappears on the orthogonal axis, and the monopole it leaves behind is consistent with zero. The 4-pass block null cannot resolve below p = 0.176 and says so. The one thing to hold loosely is hi_minus_lo: the arm order was not alternated, so that number is an upper bound on the result-path contribution. Nothing here reaches the page's E-D7 as written, and tier 2 was never allowed to.

desk.what: The §1 history describes runs that never happened. The only 12 Oct artefact is a *plan* (`reports/auto/2026-10/2026-10-12-bitflip-heat-followup-plan.md`); neither cited slug exists; "27.7 W", "45.7 W", "18.0 W" appear nowhere in the lab repo or gyroscope `reports/**`. The measured anchor is 38.29 → 63.40 W board, +18.26 W on the minion rail. A counted toggle is 0.121 fJ / 2,900 e⁻, not 15.6–18.6 fJ / 189–225 k.

A `const` pass exists for 3 of 392 configurations: `fadd.pi` 12.7321, `fmul.pi` 24.8166, `fmadd.ps` 27.2341. There is **no** const measurement for any bitwise op in any of the five E46 JSON files, so the page's 9.96 / 12.10 / 13.86 / 6.80 / 13.48 are values for runs that do not exist; the two that do read 24.82 and 27.23, not 23.09 and 21.82.

`fmadd.ps` zeros → const is **+0.1470 pJ** (27.0872 → 27.2341), not +8.94 pJ. The mechanism is misattributed too: `vpu_ctrl.v`'s zero masks are all on the **tensor** path, not the 8-lane vector FMA; the real 8.8 is *watts* of TensorFMA32 register clocking. Re-measured tonight anyway (family **Z**): the page's largest single error, 20 s a pass.
`fmul.pi` and `fmadd.ps` absolutes are offset by 9.64 and 14.21 pJ (real 24.799/50.039 and 27.087/55.759) in a table whose other six rows are raw to ±0.01 pJ. Only the deltas survive.

No statistic in `manual.json` reproduces the printed ±0.12–0.30 pJ under any consistent rule; the file's own 95% intervals are 3–5× wider (fxor random ±1.0, fand zeros ±0.88). The decomposition rests on a 1.42 pJ gap carrying ±0.69 and ±0.39 pJ bars.

The operands are floats in [0.5, 2) from seed 1, not "uniform independent bits seeded from 0xdeadbeef": 9 of 32 bit positions never toggle, E[ones] = 18.167, E[transitions] = 11.944 (§0.2). Also scored on silicon tonight (family **R**).
§0.1: `OP8_VV` is invented and the quoted C is not in `enercat.c`, but the structure — 8 ops, sinks f8..f15, op i reading (f_i, f_{i+1}) — is exactly generated mode 179.

Two capacitance conventions for one quantity inside one page: hero cards 18.5 / 126 fF (E/V²), §2 37.1 / 252 fF (E/½V²); the electron counts match the halved pair, so "252 fF (407,000 electrons)" is self-contradictory (C·V/e on 252 fF is 813,690). Same slip in "8.8 fF (2.35 fJ)" — ½CV² at 0.517 V is 1.18 fJ. **We do not repeat the class of error: §8.4 computes every capacitance from the minion-rail leg and prints both conventions.**

e_out was *solved* by subtracting AND/OR from XOR, so any XOR-cell internal cost is already inside it; §2 extracts it again as a 5.6 fJ residue and §4's simulator then adds `eXorCell` a third time to every bit.

Measured 0.5791 instructions/cycle/hart at `--harts 1` → **3.558 × 10¹¹ /s** whole card, 0.579× the page's 614.4 Gops/s "1.0 IPC". The proof is internal: the page's watt figures are E46 pJ/op deltas × 6.144e11, and the same deltas × the measured rate land on the independently recorded board watts (fxor 3.31 predicted vs 3.24–3.35 measured). Also `--harts 2` costs 0.3665 per hart, so the shared front end, not the VPU, is the limit.

Six of the seven §6 rows disagree with the page's own simulator, mostly because an E46 delta wearing a "k = 0..256" label is the model's k = 128 value: E-D1 +4.52 vs 8.89 W, E-D2 +3.73 vs 8.01 W, E-D3 +4.40 vs 9.18 W, E-D4 0.6–1.4 vs 2.58 W span, E-D5 0.15–0.45 vs 0.295 W. Only E-D6 matches its simulator, and its premise is S3. Every row is still scored tonight as a prediction.

19.65 W card idle (measured ~31.8 W at 73 °C, ~36 W at 80 °C); "0.03 W power floor" is the *zeros* pattern's run-to-run repeat spread, not a sensor floor (the documented detection line is σ/precision = 3.33 W); 167 mA and 49.5 mK/W have no provenance; 3.2 mK is the camera's **20 s** figure, not its 5-minute one (1.3 mK at 60 s, 0.6 at 300 s), so E-D7 is ~5× easier than claimed and the printed number is still wrong.

1,088 minions in 34 shires, 1,024 running kernels. Worse for E-D7: the host's own `MESH` table (`main.cpp:321-327`) puts shires 0–15 in **every** mesh column (0–5, re-verified), so "West 0–15 / East 16–31" is not a spatial split and would modulate the whole die. No 16/16 vertical or horizontal cut exists; see §10.

13.148 / 13.158 / 13.661 ✓; +7.353 / +5.995 / +5.859, gap 24% ✓; six rows to ±0.01 pJ ✓; `fsll.pi` +4.657, `fswizz.ps` +5.311, `fbcx.ps` +5.237 ✓; `fadd.pi` const − zeros +0.054 ✓ (the one real const value on the page); every E-D6 bit pattern decodes, 23/24 = 95.8% ✓. C39's 2.09× is arithmetic but not a width-only comparison (the flip counts also differ 4×).

~1,050 toggles per flipped input bit is real and sourced — 21,331 counted toggles ÷ 20.3 bits on **`txfma_top`**, the tensor unit, not the vector `fmadd.ps` the page attaches it to. 8.8 fF per clocked bit is the one figure corroborated across documents; 8.0–11.8 fF per logic toggle is 9–13× the only per-toggle capacitance with a fit behind it (0.90 fF).

The split is 1.50 : 1, not 6.81 : 1; the sum (50.90 fJ) was the only thing the catalogue ever fixed, and the page got it to 98% while splitting it wrongly. 0.517 V is aifoundry2's 21 Sep point; the only clock-pinned card is aifoundry3 at 0.522 V, and the page puts every run on aifoundry2, which is governor-free at 800 MHz / 0.617 V (C59 again).

Paths are right and "zero firmware changes" is right — tonight's build tests it. But "extend `enercat.c` with op_id 31..42" does not describe this harness: bodies are generated into an `.inc` and dispatched by name, the catalogue already holds 392 configurations, and four of the page's experiments need no new kernel at all because `--operands file:<256 B>` already exists.
